messages:
max: noticing churn on binpack nodes in us-west2 — lots of tiny inference pods bouncing and occasional OOMKilled sidecars. Looks like scheduler is packing GPUs unevenly.

anya: any FailedScheduling events? sounds like fragmentation — tiny pods should fill holes.

max: one example: 
``` 
Warning FailedScheduling 2m default-scheduler 0/24 nodes are available: 14 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 10 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

max: but `kubectl get nodes -l pool=binpack-usw2 -o wide` shows many nodes with 1-2 free GPUs.

sylvie: are these nodes mixed GPU types? recent provisioning included a mix of A100s and T4s and we added label `gpu.family` for scoring. If the pods request `gpu.memory` or a model-specific `nodeSelector` it might be rejecting T4s.

anya: check pod spec for resourceLimits/requests and nodeAffinity. max, paste one yaml?

max: there's nothing explicit: requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1, limits: 1. No affinity. However scheduler logs show `score: compatibility=0` for several nodes.

sylvie: that implies the scheduling extender (inference-compat) consulted a compatibility matrix and filtered nodes. Did we roll out the new compatibility matrix that bans older T4s for certain model variants?

ops-bot: Config apply: infra/scheduler/compat-matrix v2.7 deployed to us-west2 at 2026-01-12T01:14:02Z by infra-cd. Change: tightened gpu.family compatibility for flavor `inference-latency`.

max: timeline fits — pods started failing after 01:20 UTC.

anya: short-term mitigation: allow soft-fallback scoring so T4s can be used at lower score rather than blocked. That will let tiny pods land but preserve preference for A100s.

sylvie: agreed. I'll patch compat-matrix to add `allow_fallback: true` for inference-small in us-west2 and push a scheduler reload. Also add a metric `scheduler.compatibility_score` so we can monitor how many fallbacks happen.

max: rolling patch in canary now. Can we also avoid eviction storms? pods that already scheduled are getting preempted by high-priority batch jobs.

anya: what's priorityClasses being used? tiny inference should have `priority: medium` — batch jobs are `priority: high`. We can tune preemption by setting `preemptionPolicy: Never` for tiny pods if they're latency-sensitive, but that reduces packing flexibility.

sylvie: better: change scheduler scoring to prefer co-locating tiny pods on hetero T4 nodes and set `preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority` remains. We'll also add a soft anti-affinity to spread across racks to avoid network NIC saturation.

max: perf note: co-locating too many tiny pods on T4s caused NIC egress spikes earlier. We need throttles.

ops-bot: Metric alert: node/rack-r21 NIC egress > 75% for 3m on nodes with >6 tiny pods.

anya: ok merge the `allow_fallback` canary but keep preemption unchanged for 30m, and deploy score-tweak. Monitor p95 and node egress. max, capture baseline p95 and pod restart rate.

max: baseline p95 95ms (gateway), pod restart rate 0.2% over 15m.

sylvie: canary merged to scheduler-canary; reloading.

max: after reload, 48 pending -> 18 scheduled in 3m. preemption events reduced but a few batch jobs still push pods off.

anya: lowering preemption aggressiveness for batch in us-west2: change batch priority to `high`->`high-minus` (only slightly > medium). That should reduce eviction churn while keeping capacity for true-high.

sylvie: done in canary, will roll to prod in 10m if no regressions. Also opened follow-up: infra/scheduler#420 — implement per-node NIC egress weight in scoring to avoid overloading nodes with many small inference pods.

ops-bot: Incident note: INC-2026-0104 — binpack fragmentation causing tiny-pod churn in us-west2. Actions: compat-matrix fallback, priority tuning, NIC-aware scoring.

max: status after 30m: pending -> 0, gateway p95 98ms, restart rate 0.25% (slight increase), NIC hotspots smoothed. Closing thread but logging follow-ups.
